correctness.rationale: For all primes p>=3 and positive part sizes, F=E(J-I)S and B=(J-I)D are checked exactly. Group-by-residue H is B-invariant semisimple; quotient dimension <=p, and if dimension p the zero-residue column vanishes, proving nonzero Jordan lengths <=p and zero lengths <=p+2 in the full map. All nonzero eigenvalues have extension degree <=p-1, yielding p*LCM periods and the global iterate identity. Congruent residues give a=0 square-zero case or scalar-plus-rank-one decomposition, with exact weighted periodic-point pairs. Uniform image fibers give the entire joint transient/period count. Exhaustive programs match 87,400 vertex states and 473,295 residue-core states; finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The uniform graph-size-independent p-square period obstruction is a natural structural invariant unavailable for general finite linear networks. It follows from a bounded residue-quotient decomposition intrinsic to complete multipartite graphs, not a parameter rename. The congruent-residue family adds full primitive orbit and entry-time counts, with a sharp criterion for characteristic-divisible cycles. This resolves a natural recurrent-state classification beyond finite small-graph enumeration; universality of the numerical bound is not confused with sharpness.
